newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine hires consultants to privatise lamp plant.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine hires consultants to privatise lamp plant.

text.p: Ukraine's state privatisation agency has hired a Western consulting group to find a buyer for a lamp company, the first of 208 enterprises being offered for strategic investment tender, the agency said on Wednesday.

Ernst and Young, Vienna-based financial advisory group EPIC, its Ukrainian banking arm KINTO Securities and Investments, and law firm Squire, Sanders and Dempsey, will help Ukraine sell a 51 percent stake in the plant, it said in a statement.

KPMG was to have conducted the sale of AT Poltavsky Zavod Hasorozryadnykh Lamp but the international consulting firm failed to agree a price with the State Property Fund, KPMG senior manager Peter de Vreede told Reuters.

"We did not conclude a contract with the State Property Fund because the conditions were unacceptable," de Vreede said, adding that the government had been insisting on paying KPMG only when a buyer was found.
The Fund's statement did not say when the tender, which carries investment obligations, would take place.

"The Consultancy Group together with the SPF intend to make the Poltava tender a bench-mark transaction, setting the standard for efficiency and transparency in Ukrainian privatisation," the statement said.
The factory requested privatisation in an effort to attract funds and expertise at the plant, which employs 3,500 people in the eastern Ukrainian city of Poltava.
Ukraine is seeking to raise $1 billion in much-needed foreign investment to upgrade old factories.
Other strategic enterprises up for sale include a car maker, an alumina plant, a pulp and paper mill, steel companies and a bus manufacturer. --Irene Marushko, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
